description: SASRec predicts the next item by applying causal self-attention to a user's interaction history. Learned item and position embeddings pass through attention and feed-forward blocks with residual connections, normalization, and dropout. Candidate scores are dot products between sequence features and shared item embeddings. Training uses next-item supervision with sampled negatives. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781)
motivation: Attention can select relevant recent actions while retaining access to longer histories, balancing the simplicity of Markov models with broader sequential context. The supplied idea establishes a baseline; it specifies no additional cold-start mechanism. My assessment is that users with no history and items without training interactions remain limitations.
implementation_notes: Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset and retain separate routing for Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, and CDs_and_Vinyl. Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and the environment's 200-epoch default. Preserve the provided splits and select using macro validation HR@10 under the pinned evaluator. Store artifacts beneath the trial directory and synchronize any architecture changes with the predictor writer. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), including measured metrics and definitions. Adapt probes to the actual trained module and available interaction/title/description/timestamp data. No experiments or benchmark results are reported here.
pseudocode:
For each category:
  Load the fixed split using the baseline preprocessing.
  Initialize a category-specific SASRec model with training seed 42.
  For each training batch:
    Encode padded item sequences with positional embeddings and causal attention.
    Score shifted positive items and sampled negative items.
    Compute binary cross-entropy on nonpadding targets and update parameters.
  Save weights, configuration, and item mappings beneath the trial directory.
Write working/predict.py through the predictor writer, preserving category routing.
Use the host's fixed validation protocol to compare trials by macro HR@10.
Run compatible diagnostic probes and report only measured quantities.

originality.positive: The underlying paper introduced an influential application of self-attention to sequential recommendation.
originality.negative: Score measures novelty relative to the required baseline: this proposal reuses SASRec without a specified new cold-start contribution.

future_potential.positive: Provides a foundation for testing regularization, sampling, and permitted metadata features within the shared search budget.
future_potential.negative: Any improvement requires validation; the supplied description provides no evidence of gains on these four categories.

code_difficulty.positive: On a 1–10 scale where higher means harder, baseline reuse limits implementation effort.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct masking, category mappings, predictor reconstruction, and diagnostic compatibility still require care.
